plan.title: policy: coverageDebt + checkResume in PROJECT-DEFINITION with skippable session nudge

narratives.Description: Release-born hatch and suite-stamp features must not expand to consumers as silent defaults. This story adds plan.policy.coverageDebt and plan.policy.checkResume with unset-versus-decided semantics, fail-closed defaults when unset, and a skippable session-start nudge until the project decides.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Add **project-visible** policy for coverage-debt hatch and local check-resume / CI trust boundaries in `PROJECT-DEFINITION` (`plan.policy`), plus a **skippable session-start nudge** when the policy is unset. The nudge explains **why** and **what** is being asked; skip does not decide; the next session-start ritual nags again until the project decides (or records an explicit dismiss-with-reason).

This is the **consent / SoT surface** that makes it safe to expand release-originated features (#3187 auto-hatch, #3188 fast-before-slow + suite stamp) to **consumers** as policy-gated behavior—not silent defaults.

## Motivation

- #3187 / #3188 improve release Step 5 pain (hairline hatch re-runs; full suite after small late fails).
- Expanding those behaviors to consumers without a **project decision** risks silent soft-pass, fake-green from laptop stamps, and multi-agent quality drift.
- Hatch and ship bars are **product contracts** (shared by humans + agents on the repo), not USER.md personal prefs.
- CI trust must be **per project** (and per pipeline), never per user.

## Goals

1. **Schema + defaults** in product definition for coverage-debt and check-resume.
2. **Interactive nudge** when unset: plain language why/what; presets; skippable; re-nag on next ritual until decided.
3. **Unlock matrix** for consumer expansion of release-born features once decided (see below).

## Non-goals (v1)

- CI trusting a **local** suite stamp (`ciTrustsLocalStamp` stays **false**; separate RFC to ever allow).
- Silent default-on hatch for consumers.
- Auto-filing coverage-debt issues on **deftai/directive** from a consumer tree (ledger is always **this** repo).
- Blocking headless CI / non-interactive agents on the nudge.
- Twelve-toggle wizard; prefer one bundled preset decision.

## Proposed policy shape (conceptual)

```text
plan.policy.coverageDebt:
  status: unset | decided
  mode: off | warn | hatch      # meaningful when decided
  autoFile: boolean             # only if mode=hatch; default false for consumers
  # ledger: open issues on THIS repo with coverage-debt / --allow-coverage-debt markers (#2866)

plan.policy.checkResume:
  status: unset | decided
  localStamp: off | on          # skip re-suite at same HEAD after green local suite
  ciTrustsLocalStamp: false     # FIXED false in v1
```

**Defaults when unset or missing:** treat as `mode: off`, `localStamp: off`, CI never trusts stamps. Unset is **not** the same as decided-off for **nag** purposes (unset → nag; decided off → quiet).

Framework release may keep its own Step 5 hatch path; consumer behavior is **policy-driven**, not a copy of `task release` semantics.

## Nudge content (must say)

**Why:** Long checks often fail late on small gates, or barely miss coverage. The project can fail closed, warn, or hatch with a tracked debt issue on **this** repo. Local machines may resume a suite that already passed at the same commit; CI must not trust a laptop stamp.

**What we need:** One bundled choice (not five micro-toggles in v1):

| Preset | Writes |
|---|---|
| **Strict** (recommended for most apps) | `coverageDebt.mode=off`, `checkResume.localStamp=off` (or local on only if we split—prefer both off for Strict) |
| **Hatch-aware** | `coverageDebt.mode=hatch`, `autoFile=false` by default; `localStamp` opt (recommend on for DX) |
| **Not now / Later** | Does **not** set `status=decided`; skip this session; **nag again** next session-start ritual |

**What is not being asked:** npm publish, turning off required CI, USER.md as SoT for ship bars.

**Skippable:** “Remind me next session” — no PD mode write.  
**Stop nag:** only after `status=decided` (preset write) **or** explicit dismiss-with-reason (still visible via `policy:show` / doctor).

Use deterministic-questions contract if structured (#1470): final options include Discuss and Back.

## When the nudge fires

- Session-start **mutation** / gated ritual path (same class as other policy ticklers)—not every read-only ask.
- Condition: `coverageDebt.status == unset` (and/or checkResume unset if coupled in v1 preset).
- At most **once per** cold or re-arm session-start ritual.
- Skip entirely: `.no-deft-directive`, kill-switch, non-interactive / headless CI without TTY.
- If org/template already wrote decided policy → no nudge.
- Optional: after N skips, doctor warns “policy undecided”; frequency may soften (document choice in implementation).

## Expansion matrix (after this lands)

| Feature | Expand to consumers? | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| Fast-before-slow gate ordering (#3188) | **Yes even before nudge** | Universal fail-fast UX |
| Local suite stamp resume (#3188) | **Yes when** `checkResume.localStamp=on` | Local only; CI ignores |
| Coverage hatch / auto-file (#3187-shaped) | **Yes when** `coverageDebt.mode=hatch` (+ optional autoFile) | Ledger on **consumer** issues |
| CI soft-pass hairline | Optional later; default no | Policy + workflow explicit |
| CI trusts local stamp | **Not v1** | Separate RFC |

Without this issue: hatch/resume expansion is either silent (bad) or forever maintainer-only. With it: release-born features become **opt-in project policy**.

## Acceptance

- [ ] PD schema documents `coverageDebt` + `checkResume` (or equivalent names) with unset vs decided semantics.
- [ ] Missing/unset → no hatch soft-pass, no local stamp skip, CI never trusts local stamps.
- [ ] Interactive session-start (mutation/ritual): if unset, show why/what + Strict / Hatch-aware / Later; Later does not mark decided.
- [ ] Strict / Hatch-aware writes PD and stops nag; `task policy:show` (or equivalent) surfaces the choice.
- [ ] Dismiss-with-reason path documented and visible to doctor/policy show.
- [ ] Headless/CI does not block on the nudge.
- [ ] Docs (QUICK-START / policy / consumer check contract): why, what, skippable, re-nag, CI trust boundary.
- [ ] Unit tests: defaults, preset writes, nag eligibility, no network in unit tests.
- [ ] Explicit non-goal test or doc: consumer tree never auto-files coverage-debt on deftai/directive.

## Implementation notes

- Prefer **Personal never weakens ship bar**: USER.md may request stricter local re-run; must not authorize hatch or CI trust.
- Align copy with Controlled English / STE-ish operator voice where docs land (#2927).
- Reuse patterns from valueFeedback enable / product-signal consent (explain, confirm, durable SoT).

## References

- #3187 — release Step 5 auto-hatch branch hairline
- #3188 — Step 5 fast-before-slow + SHA suite stamp
- #2866 — open-issue ledger hatch rules
- #3185 — v0.97.0 coverage-debt hatch example
- #2859 — file-and-merge for real defects (unchanged)
- #1470 / deterministic questions — Discuss/Back if structured menu
- Session routing / session-start ritual (#2176 / #1149) — where nudge attaches
- Discussed: hatch in PD; CI trust per project not per user; nudge unlocks consumer expansion

narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Extend plan.policy types/schema under packages/core/src/policy/ for coverageDebt (status, mode, autoFile) and checkResume (status, localStamp, ciTrustsLocalStamp fixed false). 2. Fail-closed defaults when unset in policy readers. 3. Session-start mutation/ritual nudge in packages/core/src/session/ (and staleness-tickler if that is the nudge host) with Strict / Hatch-aware / Later; Later does not set decided. 4. policy:show + doctor/checks.ts surface; unit tests under policy/ and session/; docs content/docs/consumer-check-contract.md. Verify: npm test -w @deftai/directive-core -- --run policy/ and session/. Do not edit release/* or check/orchestrator.

narrative.Acceptance: Given missing or unset coverageDebt/checkResume, when hatch or local stamp would apply, then both are off and CI never trusts local stamps.
Given interactive mutation ritual and unset policy, when session-start runs, then why/what plus Strict/Hatch-aware/Later is shown; Later does not set decided and re-nags next ritual.

items.title: Presets write PD and stop nag

narrative.Acceptance: Given Strict or Hatch-aware, when chosen, then PD is written, status=decided, and the nudge stops; policy:show surfaces the choice.

Given headless/CI, when ritual runs, then nudge does not block; unit tests cover defaults/presets/eligibility; docs cover trust boundary and non-goal that consumers never auto-file debt on deftai/directive.
